newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: United Overseas to merge Malaysian units.
newsitem.headline: United Overseas to merge Malaysian units.

text.p: Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd (UOB) said on Thursday it plans to merge its two Malaysian banking units by the end of the first quarter of 1997.
In a statement, UOB said the merged units will have merged assets of 10.3 billion ringgit.
UOB's two units in Malaysia are Chung Khiaw Bank (Malaysia) Bhd with 16 branches and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd with another nine branches.
The merged entity will qualify as a Tier-1 bank under Malaysia's two-tier banking system, the statement said. Tier-1 banks are allowed a more liberal operating environment.
As at June 30, 1996, total loans and advances of Chung Khiaw and UOB Malaysia amounted to 5.9 billion ringgit.
Shareholders' funds of the two units totalled 839 million ringgit, the Singapore bank said.
The merged entity is expected to retain the name of United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd.

The equity structure of the merged units was not mentioned in the statement. UOB chairman Wee Cho Yaw is scheduled to hold a news conference in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday morning to talk about future plans of the two Malaysian units.
The UOB statement said the bank was also starting a joint venture stockbroking company with Affin Holdings Bhd.
Financial services firm Affin has said previously it would have a 55 equity in the planned joint company and UOB the remaining 45 percent.
